methodology: Articles sourced from Virginia-specific RSS feeds and Google News RSS, filtered for AI/technology/workforce relevance, then assessed by Claude against the scenario framework. Each article is tagged with the region it most affects and the scenario it signals toward.

signals.title: Roanoke College launches WorkAI Lab to prepare leaders for new era of technology - Roanoke College
signals.signal_reading: Roanoke College's WorkAI Lab represents distributed capacity-building infrastructure outside major metros, potentially creating peer learning networks that spread deep AI fluency beyond the NoVA concentration zone.

signals.title: ‘Shaping our future’: Company powering AI data centers invests $50+ million in Henrico, adding 200 jobs - WWBT
signals.signal_reading: A $50M+ AI data center infrastructure investment in Henrico reinforces Richmond's position as a secondary hub, but signals concentration in established metro corridors rather than distribution to rural regions like Southside or Southwest.

signals.title: VT Science Corner: Designing better battery technology with X-rays and AI - Roanoke Times
signals.signal_reading: Virginia Tech's AI-driven battery research demonstrates deep technical capability emerging in the New River Valley corridor, suggesting research institutions can seed distributed excellence if knowledge transfers to regional industry and workforce.

signals.title: Virginia's best-paying jobs are most exposed to AI, report says - Axios
signals.signal_reading: High-paying jobs concentrated in metro areas face AI displacement risk while lacking evidence of distributed reskilling infrastructure, signaling neither depth of AI capability nor breadth of workforce adaptation across Virginia's regions.

signals.title: AI may have limitations when illustrating smaller, rural cities - WVTF
signals.signal_reading: AI's inability to accurately represent smaller rural cities reveals both training data bias and the risk that AI tools built elsewhere fail to serve Virginia's rural regions, reinforcing rather than bridging the capability divide.
